rationales.quote: do you have any signed orders, or is it just verbal commitments at this point?
rationales.explanation: Phil seeks to distinguish committed commercial traction from preliminary verbal interest.

rationales.quote: These are paid internships?
rationales.explanation: Phil clarifies the payment structure underlying the internship model.

rationales.quote: the companies, the tech companies, the startups, are paying you to do the search?
rationales.explanation: Phil investigates who pays for the initial recruiting service.

rationales.quote: How much are they paying you to do the search?
rationales.explanation: Phil asks about the price of the initial search service.

rationales.quote: Per position?
rationales.explanation: Phil clarifies the unit on which the search fee is charged.

rationales.quote: I'd like to understand why.
rationales.explanation: Phil asks for the rationale behind charging the employer a premium fee.

rationales.quote: Are you able to decipher that?
rationales.explanation: Phil tests whether Shift can operationally translate military experience into employer-relevant skills.

rationales.quote: How do you get that information from, from the service member or from his resume?
rationales.explanation: Phil asks how the information required for the translation process is obtained.

rationales.quote: a pool of untapped, unaccessible, inaccessible talent
rationales.explanation: Phil identifies employer access to otherwise unreachable talent as a real market need.

rationales.quote: They're hard to get to, hard to access.
rationales.explanation: Phil reinforces that the target talent pool is difficult for companies to reach.

rationales.quote: Hard to translate. They don’t know what their experience was.
rationales.explanation: Phil describes employers' difficulty interpreting veterans' experience as a genuine problem.

rationales.quote: So how do you help us?
rationales.explanation: Phil asks how the solution converts military experience into value for a company like Uber.

rationales.quote: this helps them access a whole
rationales.explanation: Phil argues that the employer benefit extends beyond goodwill to practical access to talent.

rationales.quote: a new pool of talent.
rationales.explanation: Phil completes the argument that employers gain access to a new talent pool.

rationales.quote: How built out is the tech, though?
rationales.explanation: Phil asks how developed and operational the technology currently is.

rationales.quote: One of the challenges is that every year you have a new crop of 300,000 people
rationales.explanation: Phil flags the recurring challenge that each cohort may require finding new value after the transition period.

rationales.quote: You can't just rely on the services for that transition period.
rationales.explanation: Phil warns that the business cannot depend solely on one-time transition services.

rationales.quote: There has to be some continuum of services so that you can tap into the ongoing value of the email list
rationales.explanation: Phil identifies continuing services as the path to monetizing the audience beyond initial placement.

rationales.quote: you can build a rich database about these folks and really market to them a whole range of services.
rationales.explanation: Phil sees recurring service sales to a developed veteran database as an expansion of the model.

rationales.quote: If you build that data set out, could be very, very valuable.
rationales.explanation: Phil views the accumulated data set as a potentially valuable strategic asset.

rationales.quote: It's a great mission.
rationales.explanation: Phil explains his support by aligning with Shift's mission to help service members.

Extract material questions, concerns, supporting arguments and explicit investment-decision explanations. A neutral factual
question is queried/neutral, not a negative belief. Greetings, jokes, biography, simple confirmations and bare In/Out without
a reason are not rationales. Distinguish closely related taxonomy definitions; do not add broad redundant labels.
Retain each distinct rationale-bearing target utterance and exact evidence turn. Multiple labels on a turn are allowed only
when distinct concepts are expressed. For a repeated concept in different substantive turns retain each occurrence.
Quotes must be exact nonempty substrings of that turn's attributed_text, never continuation narration or another speaker.

Classify timing: original_pitch includes Q&A AND the entire original in-room decision discussion; later_commentary includes
post-pitch interviews, later diligence and subsequent updates; teaser is an opening preview/repeated future clip. Use unclear
when timing is uncertain. Do not use the redacted input cutoff as the end of original in-room discussion. Same-session
reversals stay original_pitch. Immediate investor-only debrief in the same room after the founder exits also stays
original_pitch; it is NOT later_commentary. Reserve later_commentary for separate interviews, diligence or updates. Do not mix retrospective opinions into original-pitch scoring.
Direction is positive/negative/neutral towards investing in this company. Salience primary means a stated major reason, not
merely any question. decision_link supports_in/out ONLY if the target links the rationale to the commitment/refusal.
Confidence concerns the annotation, not investment probability. Return reviewed_target_turns containing EVERY supplied target
turn index exactly once, even when it contains no rationale. An empty rationale list is valid if none was expressed.
Be concise: prefer one short exact quote per distinct concept/turn, and a one-sentence explanation. Never claim human validation.
